title: RAW UNREVIEWED: written reference elaboration tracks competing visible referents rather than total object count
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Combine historically attested deictic diagram inscriptions with the existing Voynich inventory of local labels, label families and distinct physical hosts. Hypothesize that some longer related complete forms or written qualifiers resolve competition between otherwise eligible pictured referents. The specific contrast is two similar eligible objects versus two visibly different objects: equal total count, different reference ambiguity. No Voynich form is assigned THIS, OTHER, a number, or an object name.

design.mechanism: An author can save repeated descriptions when the drawing supplies a uniquely selectable referent, but must elaborate a reference when another eligible pictured object competes. This predicts the production of written distinguishing information rather than simply a longer text on a busier page. A fixed nomenclator instead assigns the same object category the same lexical name independent of current competing objects.

positive_inputs.fact: Three Ashmole399 f13v short inscriptions visibly say similiter hic alongside nominal wording. A short inscription can therefore depend on local graphic/reference context; these are three sites on one source leaf, not independent replication.

Existing detailed inventory separates ten panels, thirteen records and 28 component-label tokens, including related complete label forms and single-, paired- and multiple-object settings. Old source/direction glosses in that report are not imported.
Ten exact label/prose bridges cross physical panel owners. Reuse exists but does not establish referent identity; the corrected ownership inventory is available independently of a target translation.

design.unit: Complete previously admitted and already inventoried panels plus all their labels and full attached prose records. Independently code a finite visible object-class criterion and all compatible distractors, keeping one versus multiple depicted instances separate from same versus different class. No new images or manuscript contents are authorized by this card.
design.contrast: CONTRASTIVE_REFERENCE: a finite qualifier removes a specified compatible competitor from the eligible referent set; FIXED_CATEGORY_NAME: whole-form identity depends on object class but not the current competitor set; TOTAL_COUNT: added wording depends only on number of drawn objects or available space. All are restricted working mechanisms, not exhaustive theories of deixis or naming.
design.prediction: At matched total object count and label/prose position, contrastive reference requires a written distinction only when its declared eligible referent set otherwise contains more than one candidate. That qualifier must select the same relative property in the next independently nominated complete case; its contribution cannot be chosen separately per panel. Different-class extra objects do not trigger the same predicted elaboration. Fixed-category and count-only models make different predictions for these crossed cells.
design.falsifier: A frozen qualifier account fails when two still-eligible competitors survive its complete written description, or when the same qualifier selects contradictory relative properties across complete cases. Mere increased word length or more labels on crowded drawings is insufficient. If a picture supplies no reliable eligible set, record ambiguity rather than count a success.
design.smallest_next_step: Using only the already preserved panel and label-host inventory, nominate one two-similar versus two-different crossed comparison, retaining all labels rather than picking one attractive pair. Before further payload inspection, write finite candidate-set eliminations for the full reference constructions, with fixed atomic-name and count-only rivals. This is concrete exploratory authoring; do not build an ambiguity classifier or new visual annotation system. If that particular comparison is absent, retain this raw idea without a new missing-input experiment.
design.predecessors: IDEA26 tests reset at panel boundaries; this holds boundaries and total count fixed while changing the number of eligible competitors. IDEA57 tests caption/prose arity; this predicts which extra information resolves a specific competitor. IDEA893 distinguishes part/name/topic using context transport; IDEA897 tests participant-conditioned r/l phrase patterns. None of those consequences is asserted to have passed here. GDT1153 prior-occurrence rule remains contradicted; the proposed visible-competitor test is not a repair of its selected loci. GDT793 strict ordinal and GDT794 position-transfer failures remain; no rank, compass position or numeral is assigned. IDEA77 concerns singular/plural cardinality; here total cardinality is matched and the varying quantity is competitor compatibility. IDEA896 tests a fixed p/y rendering/reference commute; this candidate requires no p/y change and predicts added distinguishing content from the visible competitor set.
design.limits: Referential uniqueness is a proposed authoring convention, not established Voynich grammar. Similar-looking objects need not be semantically identical; labels may name classes, actions, places or instances. Source similiter hic does not prove a corresponding target convention. No existing longer form is automatically segmented as a modifier; the directed-composition and whole-form-residual constraints remain. Global exact-word profiles and prior counterexamples are required before any concrete candidate values. All reader channels remain separate; all exposure disclosed; f84/f84r and reserves closed.
